prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot to Shore Control Room), Main Transformer (loading/temp monitored; abnormal trend escalated; protection settings separately approved), export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory to Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; Dispatcher sets permitted export; relay applies ceiling, keeps protection unless authorized switching plan). Public grid, port out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms to Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel (alarms used with on-site reports), Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace to Substation Operator; readiness checked), Helideck (evacuation only if aviation, deck, receiving acceptable). Substation Operator: switching, clearances after authorization. Control Engineer: one-action steps, hold points, verifies limits, stepwise reduction/restore, confirms software changes, remote shutdown when safe. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint (Duty Planner handover records), Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarm priority safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt to Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment; incident log, single offshore point of contact), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale), Work Permit Portal (Isolation Boundary Sketch), Operations Radio Console (Control Room-vessels-teams), Warehouse System. Weather Service (forecast), Metocean Buoy (site measurements), Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note to Duty Planner; uncertainty changes to Rescue Coordinator). Personnel counts: Marine Coordinator sets expected count (Berth Slot Confirmation), confirms reconciliation, tracks vessels/marine support; Vessel Master (Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction to Personnel Tracking Console; vessel safety/approach authority); incident lead verifies headcounts. Crew Transfer Vessel suspended beyond limits; Daughter Craft if suitable; Service Operations Vessel (Recovery Basket Load Sheet; accommodation/medical); North/South Access

New part:
S634: If conditions exceed the approved operating envelope, the Vessel Master may withdraw and the Rescue Coordinator revises the response plan.
S635: After an incident, personnel are accounted for, hazards are reassessed, and restart authority is assigned before normal work resumes.
S636: Vessel recovery support coordinates people, vessels, and handling equipment before any offshore recovery begins.
S637: The Rescue Coordinator establishes the recovery objective and confirms who has authority to suspend the operation.
S638: The Marine Coordinator assigns suitable vessels and maintains a common plan for their approach and departure.
S639: The Duty Planner confirms that the recovery task does not conflict with other offshore work.
S640: The Weather Service provides current forecasts for the recovery area and the planned transit route.
S641: The Weather Analyst interprets forecast uncertainty and identifies conditions that could affect safe vessel handling.
S642: The Vessel Master retains authority over vessel movements and may decline a task that cannot be completed safely.
S643: The Crew Transfer Vessel transports personnel and small equipment only when sea conditions and transfer arrangements are acceptable.
S644: The Daughter Craft may be assigned close-in support when its operating limits and communications coverage are adequate.
S645: The Service Operations Vessel provides a stable working platform when the response requires additional deck space or lifting capability.
S646: The Rescue Coordinator uses the load sheet to confirm that recovery baskets are secured and their contents are accounted for before transfer.
S647: The HSE Officer reviews the handling method, lifting points, and exclusion zones before loads are moved.
S648: The Personnel Tracking Console supports confirmation that all assigned personnel have returned to a safe location.
S649: The Field Supervisor maintains control of the work area and stops handling if personnel enter a restricted zone.
S650: The Electrical Technician isolates and protects recovered electrical equipment before it is placed in temporary storage.
S651: The Blade Specialist identifies fragile blade components and specifies padding or restraints to prevent handling damage.
S652: Recovered equipment is kept separated from loose debris and is secured against sliding, impact, and spray exposure.
S653: Damaged or contaminated items are contained so that they cannot create hazards for personnel or other cargo.
S654: Lifting gear is inspected before use, and each lift is conducted within the rated capacity of the equipment.
S655: The Warehouse System is used to arrange receiving space and preserve traceability for equipment returned ashore.
S656: The Spares Hub is consulted when recovered components may be needed to support repair planning.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
